en.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon for robot control, simulation, and policy optimization
en.summary:
Google releases Gemini 4 Argon for robot control, simulation and policy optimization

Gemini 4 Argon is Google's general-purpose physical reasoning model focused on embodied AI tasks, supporting robot control, Real2Sim scene reconstruction, video annotation and policy optimization. It scores 87% on pure reasoning in the ERQA benchmark, with real-world task success rates rising from 56% to 75%. The model is available through the Gemini API and Google AI Ultra.

Trained in MuJoCo, Argon can drive Spot to complete a foot-pedal task; it supports robotic arm control via visual coordinates and HTTP motion primitives; and it enables domain randomization from a single image.
en.reason: Google's Gemini 4 Argon, a general physical reasoning model for embodied tasks, scores 87% pure reasoning on the ERQA benchmark and lifts real-world task success from 56% to 75%, while supporting robot control, Real2Sim reconstruction, video annotation and policy optimization.

Coding Agent is advancing into an engineering collaborator that understands codebases, runs tests, and delivers work alongside teams.

en.title: GPT-6.2 Is More Powerful and Cheaper—So Why Are People Still Complaining?
en.summary:
GPT-6.2 Is Stronger and Cheaper—So Why Are People Still Bashing It?

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol finally quietly went live in the early hours this morning (word had been circulating for two months). Astra is the flagship, while Sol is the daily workhorse for coding. Both are already visible in Work on the web and in the Codex client.

On one side are polished car webpages, 3D models, and a bill that is hard not to look at twice: in OpenAI's published professional-task benchmark results, Astra costs $2.89 per task, while Claude Fable 5.2 costs $60.05.

On the other, several developers who used it early are complaining: it cannot explain things clearly, stops halfway through a task, and in the end a human has to come back and clean up.

Like this guy, whose complaint is already approaching a million reads.

Lao Jin reviewed the official materials, independent evaluations, and the first batch of community feedback together.

@Layton showcased a car: against a dark background, the body, glass roof, and lighting together give it a premium feel.

He said the result took only one minute, and he also published the detailed prompt he used. His instructions to the model were very specific—not just casually throwing out "make a good-looking website." Everyone should learn this; I have said it hundreds of times—don't just...
en.reason: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra costs $2.89 per task against Claude Fable 5.2's $60.05 in professional evaluations, yet early developers report it stops mid-task and needs human cleanup, a piece weighing official benchmarks against first-hand complaints.

Title: 从 Trellis 看 AI 研发工具选型：OpenSpec、Spec Kit 与 Harness 如何配合
Published Time: 2026-11-17T06:02:12+00:00
**OpenSpec、Spec Kit 与 Harness：理清关系，再选 AI 研发工具**
同时使用 Codex、Cursor 和 Claude Code 后，团队很容易遇到三类问题：
*   同一个项目，在不同工具里维护了不同版本的规则。
*   需求已经说过，AI 实现时仍然遗漏关键场景。
*   任务做到一半，换个会话后又要重新解释进度。
这些问题彼此相关，却需要不同的解决办法。Rulesync、Spec Kit、OpenSpec、Trellis，以及经常被提到的 Harness，就分别涉及其中的不同环节。
**一、先分清：规范、规范工具和 Harness**
“项目宪法”通常记录长期工程原则，例如架构边界、依赖管理、测试要求；具体功能的 Spec 则描述本次要实现的行为、边界条件和验收标准。

en.title: AI dev tool selection through Trellis: how OpenSpec, Spec Kit, and Harness work together
en.summary:
Choosing AI Development Tools Through Trellis: How OpenSpec, Spec Kit, and Harness Work Together

OpenSpec, Spec Kit, and Harness: Sort Out the Relationships Before Choosing AI Development Tools

Once teams use Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code together, they can easily run into three types of problems:

* The same project ends up with different versions of rules maintained in different tools.
* Requirements have already been stated, yet the AI implementation still misses key scenarios.
* A task is halfway done, but after switching to a new session, progress has to be explained all over again.

These problems are related, but they call for different solutions. Rulesync, Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Trellis, and the frequently mentioned Harness each address a different part of the process.

1. First, Distinguish Specs, Spec Tools, and Harness

A project constitution typically records long-term engineering principles, such as architectural boundaries, dependency management, and testing requirements; a spec for a specific feature describes the behavior, boundary conditions, and acceptance criteria to be implemented this time.

Spec Kit and OpenSpec are tools that help teams organize this material and move development forward.
en.reason: Teams running Codex, Cursor and Claude Code together hit duplicated rule versions, missed scenarios and lost session progress, and this piece uses a voice-chat-room auto-reconnect case to separate what Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Harness, Trellis and Rulesync each handle.

en.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon for robot control, simulation, and policy optimization
en.summary:
Google releases Gemini 4 Argon for robot control, simulation and policy optimization

Gemini 4 Argon is Google's general-purpose physical reasoning model focused on embodied AI tasks, supporting robot control, Real2Sim scene reconstruction, video annotation and policy optimization. It scores 87% on pure reasoning in the ERQA benchmark, with real-world task success rates rising from 56% to 75%. The model is available through the Gemini API and Google AI Ultra.

Trained in MuJoCo, Argon can drive Spot to complete a foot-pedal task; it supports robotic arm control via visual coordinates and HTTP motion primitives; and it enables domain randomization from a single image.
en.reason: Google's Gemini 4 Argon, a general physical reasoning model for embodied tasks, scores 87% pure reasoning on the ERQA benchmark and lifts real-world task success from 56% to 75%, while supporting robot control, Real2Sim reconstruction, video annotation and policy optimization.

en.title: Context Management Practices from the Volcano Engine Agent-Native Team | AICon Beijing
en.summary:
Word count: 1,785
Reading time: about 6 minutes

Agent has evolved from a Q&A tool into an enterprise-grade worker that understands goals, calls systems, and executes in a closed loop — and engineering capability has become the key bottleneck to scaling it.

Model capability sets the ceiling; toolchain, context management, execution environment, and feedback-loop design determine whether an Agent is production-ready. Enterprises are shifting their focus to task fit, acceptance criteria for results, and control of permissions, cost, and risk. Coding Agent is advancing into an engineering collaborator that understands codebases, runs tests, and delivers work alongside teams.

Intended for AI platform engineers, MLOps engineers, and enterprise architects.

When Agent truly enters enterprise workflows, which work can be handed to AI? 50+ real-world cases reveal the answer.

AI is moving from an assistant that answers questions to a worker that understands goals, calls systems, and completes tasks. Once Agent enters enterprise workflows, the question is no longer "how do we build AI" but which work can be handed to AI, how results are accepted, and how permissions, cost, and risk are contained. As LLMs extend into reasoning, tool calling, multimodality, and long-horizon tasks, development focus is shifting from single calls to the design of context, tools, execution environments, and feedback loops. Coding Agent, too, has evolved from code completion into an engineering collaborator that understands codebases, runs tests, and completes complex tasks. OpenAI, Google C

en.title: GPT-6.2 Is More Powerful and Cheaper—So Why Are People Still Complaining?
en.summary:
GPT-6.2 Is Stronger and Cheaper—So Why Are People Still Bashing It?

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol finally quietly went live in the early hours this morning (word had been circulating for two months). Astra is the flagship, while Sol is the daily workhorse for coding. Both are already visible in Work on the web and in the Codex client.

On one side are polished car webpages, 3D models, and a bill that is hard not to look at twice: in OpenAI's published professional-task benchmark results, Astra costs $2.89 per task, while Claude Fable 5.2 costs $60.05.

On the other, several developers who used it early are complaining: it cannot explain things clearly, stops halfway through a task, and in the end a human has to come back and clean up.

Like this guy, whose complaint is already approaching a million reads.

Lao Jin reviewed the official materials, independent evaluations, and the first batch of community feedback together.

@Layton showcased a car: against a dark background, the body, glass roof, and lighting together give it a premium feel.

He said the result took only one minute, and he also published the detailed prompt he used. His instructions to the model were very specific—not just casually throwing out "make a good-looking website." Everyone should learn this; I have said it hundreds of times—don't just...
en.reason: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra costs $2.89 per task against Claude Fable 5.2's $60.05 in professional evaluations, yet early developers report it stops mid-task and needs human cleanup, a piece weighing official benchmarks against first-hand complaints.

en.title: AI dev tool selection through Trellis: how OpenSpec, Spec Kit, and Harness work together
en.summary:
Choosing AI Development Tools Through Trellis: How OpenSpec, Spec Kit, and Harness Work Together

OpenSpec, Spec Kit, and Harness: Sort Out the Relationships Before Choosing AI Development Tools

Once teams use Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code together, they can easily run into three types of problems:

* The same project ends up with different versions of rules maintained in different tools.
* Requirements have already been stated, yet the AI implementation still misses key scenarios.
* A task is halfway done, but after switching to a new session, progress has to be explained all over again.

These problems are related, but they call for different solutions. Rulesync, Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Trellis, and the frequently mentioned Harness each address a different part of the process.

1. First, Distinguish Specs, Spec Tools, and Harness

A project constitution typically records long-term engineering principles, such as architectural boundaries, dependency management, and testing requirements; a spec for a specific feature describes the behavior, boundary conditions, and acceptance criteria to be implemented this time.

Spec Kit and OpenSpec are tools that help teams organize this material and move development forward.
en.reason: Teams running Codex, Cursor and Claude Code together hit duplicated rule versions, missed scenarios and lost session progress, and this piece uses a voice-chat-room auto-reconnect case to separate what Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Harness, Trellis and Rulesync each handle.
